content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: multiple containers on gpu-45 failed with CUDA illegal memory access (possible misaligned pointer) across P0 serving runtime. Autoscale halted for the pool.

oncall-ai: I'm on it — paging SRE/Runtime. Dropping into triage channel.

sre-aly: seeing repeated 'invalid device address' in container logs. cpu/gpu saturations look normal, memory pressure spikes right before the crash.

runtime-eng-ben: logs show this pattern: kernel pointer read at offset 0x18 causing address to jump. probably a kernel/SMMU translation edge-case. attaching snippet.

runtime-eng-ben: ```
E 03:21:03 service/runtime.c:427 handle_request() 
   cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f9a2c8e12f0 (pc 0x7f9a2c8e1300)
   stack: ... serving-runtime v3.4.1+hotpatch
```

mlops-jordan: traffic profile: burst of long-context chat completions with batch_size=48 on this pool. batch queue shows many concurrent prefix hits.

support-lina: any customer impact yet? we have two support tickets mentioning short 5-10s 500s from our hosted API. customer-ops says some customers saw degraded streams.

infra-ops-raj: I'm cordoning gpu-45 and draining pods from that node. will move running jobs to fallback pool (cpu-fallback-1 & gpu-legacy).

oncall-ai: action plan: 1) cordon+drain node; 2) rollback serving-runtime to v3.4.0 on the pool; 3) enable model-variant fallback (small-quant) for affected customers; 4) capture full core dump & nvml traces.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: rollback serving-runtime pool 'inference-pool-3' to v3.4.0 — initiated by oncall-ai. Progress: 30% (8/24 pods).

runtime-eng-ben: also change routing policy: prefer 'gpu-legacy' for new requests while we investigate. That's a config flip in the router (5s downtime risk).

mlops-jordan: enabling prefix-cache bypass for high-concurrency endpoints to reduce KV cache churn. Will flip under Canary.

infra-ops-raj: drain complete on gpu-45, cordoned. No more new pods scheduled. Migrations to fallback pools are in progress.

support-lina: drafted customer notice for impacted tenants: short blip, some 500s, failover in progress. Share for review: "We observed transient errors affecting streaming responses for a subset of requests. Our engineers are actively failing over workloads and applying a rollback to stabilize. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation."

customer-ops: please include affected models + time window. we need precise deltas for SLA credits.

mlops-jordan: affected models list: com.redwood/longchat-v2, open/llama-extended-13b; window: 03:20-03:40 UTC approx.

sre-aly: still seeing occasional OOM-ish traces in older nodes that took over traffic. increasing mem limits for the runtime container to +200Mi as temporary measure.

runtime-eng-ben: core dump captured. nvprof shows a pagewalk failure followed by illegal deviceaddr read. hypothesis: kernel TLB eviction race when large KV cache prefix is rehydrated during batch scheduling.

oncall-ai: good. next steps: preserve dumps, escalate to kernel team if repro. For live mitigation: keep rollout at v3.4.0, keep routing to gpu-legacy, and set max_batch_size=24 cluster-wide for 1 hour.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete on inference-pool-3. All pods now at v3.4.0, health checks passing.

infra-ops-raj: switching router weights: gpu-legacy +30%, inference-pool-3 -30% (gradual over 10s).

support-lina: customer notice sent to impacted tenants (channels: email & status). Template included incident window and immediate mitigations.

customer-ops: customers acknowledged; one large tenant requested ETA — provided best-effort 2hr remediation window.

runtime-eng-ben: started a short repro: synthetic load with long prefix + concurrent batch joins. If we can repro consistently, we'll try a hotfix to prevent invalid pointer deref (add sanity check around deviceaddr path).

sre-aly: oncall handing to night-shift: @oncall-ai -> @infra-ops-raj for 03:45 UTC onward. please maintain mitigations and alert if error rate rises above 0.5% for more than 5m.

oncall-ai: handing off logs, core dumps, nvml traces, and rollback timeline to infra-ops-raj in #incident-archive.

infra-ops-raj: acked. I'll keep the node cordoned until kernel-level repro is ruled out. Scheduling deeper tracing tomorrow with kernel team.

support-lina: closing loop with customers for now. Will update postmortem doc with impact table and messages.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> service degraded. Follow-up: assigned to runtime-eng-ben for RCA and to infra-ops-raj for kernel coordination. Postmortem due in 72 hours.

runtime-eng-ben: quick note for RCA: collect allocation stack traces + SMMU logs; consider adding serialization on prefix rehydrate path and bounds-check for deviceaddr offset.

sre-aly: thanks everyone. summary: illegal deviceaddr reads causing container crashes during high-concurrency long-context batches; mitigation: node cordon/drain, runtime rollback, route shift, batch size cap, mem bump. moving to monitoring phase. :white_check_mark:
